name: Ossuary-Tide

civilization.name: The Tide Cartels
civilization.notes: A coastal mercantile culture that annihilated itself in a three-day exchange of fission weapons after its inland sea dried up.

description: Ossuary-Tide is a small rust-brown world whose surface is written in water that is no longer there: branching riverbeds etched into highlands, harbor terraces ringing a basin wide enough to have held an inland sea, all of it dry for perhaps four thousand years. At the basin's center, the flash-fused glass of the final war spreads in a smooth pale sheet that mirrors the stars at night.

The thin wind moves grit across the ruins with a sound like whispered counting. Standing on a harbor terrace, you can trace the tide-lines in the mineral staining and know exactly how slowly the water died—century by century, meter by meter. Nothing here casts a soft edge; the low sun cuts everything into hard planes and long violet shadows.

The Tide Cartels built harbor cities down the dying coast right up until they turned their arsenals on each other over the last freshwater aquifer. Ground-penetrating surveys have since found something far older beneath the glass plain: a buried megastructure predating the cartels by an unknown span, its geometry suggesting it was built either to hold water or to take it away. The cartels' own records never mention it.

Dark crystal seams run through the basin walls where the bombs struck oldest rock, and every syndicate in the sector has filed claims it cannot legally hold. But the archaeology corps has quietly petitioned to classify the whole world as a grave site—because their probes into the megastructure keep returning the same reading: something inside is still cycling water.
